rationale: Small near-expiry continuation of the authorized source work: closing the two narrow transport items left open last step and re-checking the heartbeat classification against what the leader actually emits. Reading only; no defect asserted, no obligation created.

feedback.answered: Three items are closed. In-process queueing: NewInmemTransportWithTimeout builds the transport with a consumer channel of capacity 16 and a generated address when none is given (inmem_transport.go 53-65), so up to sixteen in-process RPCs can queue in the peer's channel before a sender blocks, on top of that sender's own send timeout. Address provider: serverAddressProvider is taken once from the config at construction (net_transport.go 236) and serverAddressLock is only ever read in getProviderAddressOrFallback (389-398), so the library never mutates the provider after construction and the in-flight-dial race I listed is not a library-side concern - concurrency inside a caller-supplied provider is the caller's. Heartbeat classification: the leader's heartbeat goroutine emits an AppendEntriesRequest carrying only the RPC header, Term = s.currentTerm and the legacy leader address, with PrevLogEntry, PrevLogTerm, Entries and LeaderCommitIndex all left at zero (replication.go 388-395), which is exactly the shape the inbound transport classifies as a heartbeat (non-zero term, non-empty leader address, zero prev coordinate, no entries, zero commit index), so the fast path does fire for real heartbeats as intended.
remaining: No transport item from the previous lists remains open as a library responsibility; caller-supplied StreamLayer wrappers (including any TLS) stay outside the library.
Nothing in the transport reading was evaluated for defects, so the surface's correctness remains unmapped even though its behaviour is now mostly described.

Previously recorded open items are unchanged: installSnapshot watermark reachability from a legal leader history, the compacted-leader variant of the truncation-failure case, and execution corroboration of the two reading-based consequences.
feedback.rationale: Recorded as feedback because it completes the descriptive reading of the deferred transport surface and withdraws one item that turned out not to be a library concern; it establishes no requirement and changes no confirmed result.
